channel.title: Car Recall Tracker — new vehicle recalls
channel.description: NHTSA vehicle safety recalls explained in plain English.

item.title: Dodge Durango Tail Lights May Fail From Damaged Connections
item.description: Certain Dodge Durango vehicles may have damaged electrical connections in the tail light wiring. This damage can cause the tail lights to fail. When the tail lights do not light up properly, other drivers may have more difficulty seeing the vehicle. The vehicles fail to meet federal lighting requirements. Dealers will inspect the tail lights and replace them as necessary, free of charge.

item.title: Audi Q4 E-Tron Models Face Battery Fire Risk
item.description: Audi is recalling certain 2024-2025 Q4 E-Tron and Q4 Sportback E-Tron vehicles because their high-voltage battery may fail and cause a fire. The repair is still being developed. Until it is completed, owners are advised to charge their vehicles to no more than 80% capacity. Audi expects to mail initial safety notices on December 18, 2026, and will send additional letters when the repair is available.

item.title: Hyundai Elantra and Elantra N Wheels May Detach
item.description: Hyundai is recalling certain Elantra and Elantra N vehicles because the nuts that hold the wheels in place may loosen. A wheel could come off the vehicle. The recall also includes certain Elantra Hybrid and Venue vehicles. Dealers will inspect and tighten the wheel nuts and replace the wheel hub bearing assembly if needed. This work is free of charge.

item.title: Lexus NX Models May Fail to Display Important Warnings
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain 2022-2024 Lexus NX250, NX350, NX350 Hybrid, and NX450h+ vehicles because the dashboard display may not show some warnings or indicators. The missing information may include engine oil pressure, engine coolant temperature, or electrical charge. These vehicles do not meet the federal requirements for controls and displays. Dealers will update the display software for free. Owner notification letters are expected to be mailed December 7, 2026.

item.title: Toyota Sienna Hybrid Second-Row Seat Backs May Not Stay Secured
item.description: Toyota is recalling certain seven-passenger Sienna Hybrid vehicles because the second-row seat backs may not stay secured during a crash. An unsecured seat back may not properly protect the person sitting there. Dealers will update the software that controls the vehicle’s restraint system. For vehicles with the “Mobility as a Service” package, dealers will replace both second-row seat backs. These repairs are free.

item.title: Ford F-350 SD and F-450 SD Tailgate Cable May Fail
item.description: Ford is recalling certain F-150, F-250 SD, F-350 SD, and F-450 SD vehicles because the cable on the left side of the tailgate may fail under certain heavy loads. If it fails, the tailgate may drop onto the rear bumper. Dealers will replace the left-side cable for free. Ford plans to send owners another letter when the repair becomes available.

item.title: Hyundai Elantra Loose Suspension Fasteners May Affect Steering
item.description: The fasteners securing the front suspension strut assemblies in certain Hyundai Elantra vehicles may not have been tightened properly. This can cause the driver to lose steering control. Dealers will inspect the fasteners and replace them as necessary. They will also perform a wheel alignment as needed. The inspection, any necessary fastener replacement, and any necessary alignment are free of charge.

item.title: Subaru Crosstrek and Forester Front Suspension Joint May Separate
item.description: Certain Subaru Crosstrek and Forester vehicles may have an improperly secured nut on a joint in the left front suspension. The joint, called a ball joint, may separate from the lower suspension arm. Dealers will inspect the left front ball joint assembly and replace it if needed. Owners are advised not to drive until the repair is completed.

item.title: Porsche 911 Carrera GTS Wheel Bolt May Break
item.description: The bolt that secures the wheel at its center may break on affected Porsche vehicles, including the 911 Carrera GTS. If the bolt breaks, the wheel may come off the vehicle. Dealers will check the wheel fastening parts and replace any that were made incorrectly, as needed. Owners are advised not to drive their vehicles until the repair is complete.

item.title: Volvo VNL (4) Cabs Have Loose or Missing Bolts
item.description: Volvo Trucks is recalling certain VNL (4) trucks because bolts that hold the cab structure together may be loose or missing. If the truck crashes, the cab may not protect someone inside as it should. That increases the risk of injury. Dealers will check for missing bolts and install or tighten bolts as needed.

item.title: Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrid Fuel Connection May Leak
item.description: The fuel tube connection near the fuel tank may come apart on affected Toyota Land Cruiser Hybrid vehicles. If the connection separates, fuel may leak. Dealers will inspect the connection and add an extra clamp. If needed, they will also replace the fuel tube and install the extra clamp. The inspection will determine which of these repairs the vehicle needs.

item.title: Genesis G80 Power Seat Motors May Overheat, Catch Fire
item.description: The front power seats have motors that can overheat if the seat control switch gets stuck. This overheating can lead to a fire, and it can happen whether the vehicle is parked or being driven. The issue involves the power controls built into the front seats of these vehicles.

item.title: Volvo EX30 Head Restraint Cushion May Detach in Crash
item.description: The cushion on the head restraint attached to the seat may come loose if the vehicle is in a crash. If that happens, the head restraint may not work as intended during the crash, which can increase the chance of injury.

item.title: Honda Hybrid Tire Kit Bottle Cap May Pop Off
item.description: These vehicles come with a tire repair kit that includes a sealant bottle. When the kit is used on a flat tire, pressure can build up inside the bottle, causing the cap to detach unexpectedly. A cap that comes off this way can fly off and strike the person using the kit or someone standing nearby.

item.title: Toyota RAV4 Plug-In Hybrid May Lose Power Driving
item.description: A computer that helps run the plug-in hybrid system may run into an error. If this happens while driving at higher speeds, the hybrid system may reduce power or shut down. This can cause the vehicle to suddenly lose drive power while it is moving.

item.title: BMW R 18 Reverse Gear Unit May Overheat
item.description: On affected BMW R 18 motorcycles with the optional reverse gear, a seal on the reverse gear control unit may deteriorate. Moisture can then get inside the unit, which may overheat. Dealers will replace the reverse gear control unit. Motorcycles that already received a repair under the previous recall still need this new repair, according to the notice.

item.title: Ford Super Duty Trucks May Show Inaccurate Speed
item.description: On affected Ford trucks, the dashboard needles showing engine speed and vehicle speed may get stuck or move erratically. This can give the driver inaccurate readings. The recall includes certain F-350 SD, F-450 SD, F-550 SD and F-600 trucks, along with other listed Ford models. Dealers will replace the affected dashboard units. Owners will receive an additional letter when the repair is available.

item.title: Mercedes-Benz S 580 Brake Hose Leak Risk
item.description: Mercedes-Benz is recalling certain S 580 4MATIC and S 580 E 4MATIC vehicles because the front brake hoses may crack and leak brake fluid. When brake fluid leaks out, the brakes do not work as well, so the vehicle can take longer to come to a stop. The dealer will replace the front brake hoses to fix the problem, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Honda VT750 Motorcycle Fuel Pump Failure
item.description: Honda is recalling certain VT750 motorcycles because the fuel pump may malfunction due to a manufacturing defect. A fuel pump that fails can cause the engine to suddenly stall while the motorcycle is being ridden. Dealers will replace the fuel pump free of charge to correct the problem.

item.title: Volkswagen ID.4 High-Voltage Battery Fire Risk
item.description: Volkswagen says the high-voltage battery in certain ID.4 vehicles may fail. If the battery fails, it could lead to a vehicle fire.

item.title: Rivian R2 Loose Battery Fastener Cuts Drive Power
item.description: A fastener on the high voltage battery may not have been tightened correctly. This can cause the vehicle to lose drive power while it is being driven. Rivian will inspect the connection and repair it, or replace any damaged parts, at no cost to the owner.

item.title: Ram ProMaster Vans Risk Losing Power Steering
item.description: Chrysler says water may enter the wiring for the power steering system in certain Ram ProMaster vans, including the electric Ram 3500. If this happens, the power steering assist that helps turn the wheel can stop working.

item.title: Volvo VNL Trucks: Software Flaw Weakens Braking
item.description: In these Volvo VNL trucks, a software error can miscalculate how much weight is sitting on the truck's axles. This mistake happens when the truck is pulling certain smoothbore tanker trailers. Because the calculation is wrong, the brakes may not perform as well as they should while towing, which can affect how well and how quickly the truck is able to slow down and come to a stop.

item.title: Cadillac Optiq Power Windows May Pinch Passengers
item.description: On some Cadillac Optiq vehicles, the front power windows may not sense when something is in the way when they are closed using the key fob's express-up function. Instead of detecting the obstruction and reversing direction, the window can keep closing, which could pinch a passenger before it retracts. Because the windows don't reverse as expected in this situation, these vehicles do not meet a federal safety standard for power windows.

item.title: Ford Expedition and Super Duty Trucks: Headlight Failure
item.description: Some Ford Expedition and F-350, F-450, and F-550 Super Duty trucks have headlight assemblies that may contain a faulty LED chip. This can cause the daytime running lights, parking lights, high beams, or low beams to stop working, reducing how well other drivers can see the vehicle or how well the driver can see the road ahead at night. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet federal headlight safety requirements.

item.title: Rivian R1S and R1T backup camera display issue
item.description: In some Rivian R1S and R1T vehicles, a notification can pop up on screen and block part of the rearview camera image when the vehicle is in reverse. This can make it harder for the driver to see what is behind the vehicle while backing up.

item.title: Volkswagen Atlas And Tiguan Steering Bolt May Break
item.description: This recall covers certain Volkswagen Tiguan and Atlas SUVs, along with related Audi Q3 vehicles. A bolt that attaches the steering rack to the subframe can corrode, or rust, and break over time. If that bolt breaks, the steering rack housing itself can break as well, affecting the steering system on these vehicles. The bolt involved is located on the right side of the steering rack.

item.title: Hyundai Ioniq 9 Powered Rear Seats May Trap People
item.description: Certain Hyundai Ioniq 9 vehicles with Limited, Calligraphy, or Calligraphy Design trim have second-row powered seats that may fail to detect a person. The seats may keep moving after touching someone during powered adjustments, including automatic folding and stowing. Someone could become trapped by a moving rear seat. The notice specifically identifies children as being at risk of getting trapped and injured.

item.title: Jeep Wagoneer Roof Rack Crossbars May Come Loose
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer, and Grand Wagoneer L vehicles because the pivot bolts holding the roof rack crossbars may not have been tightened correctly. This could let the crossbars come loose and detach from the roof while the vehicle is being driven, rather than staying securely attached as intended.

item.title: Volkswagen Tiguan Software Glitch Can Stall Engine
item.description: A software error can cause the body control module in the vehicle to reset itself. This can make the ignition switch off, which then stalls the engine. The same software error can also cause a loss of certain vehicle controls, warning lights, and exterior lighting. It can also cause the rearview camera system to stop working properly, affecting several parts of the vehicle at once.

item.title: Toyota RAV4, Tundra Hybrid Weight Label Error
item.description: The label on your vehicle that shows the load carrying capacity modification may display an inaccurate added weight value. This means the number telling you how much extra weight your vehicle can carry may not be correct. Dealers will replace the load carrying capacity modification label with a corrected one, free of charge, once new labels are ready to be mailed to owners.

item.title: Jeep Grand Cherokee Rear Coil Spring May Detach
item.description: On these Jeep Grand Cherokee models, the rear coil springs may have been installed incorrectly. Because of this, a spring can come loose and separate from the vehicle while you are driving. This recall replaces two earlier recalls for the same problem, and vehicles already repaired under those earlier recalls will still need this new fix.

item.title: Jeep tire pressure warning system may miss low tires
item.description: Chrysler is recalling certain Jeep Grand Cherokee, Grand Cherokee L, Grand Cherokee 4xe, Wagoneer, Wagoneer L, Grand Wagoneer and Cherokee vehicles. A software error means the tire pressure monitoring system may not detect a tire that is low, or may not turn on the tire pressure warning light the way it should. Because of this, the vehicles do not meet the federal standard for tire pressure monitoring systems. Dealers will update the software free of charge.

item.title: Chrysler Pacifica Sensor Crack May Disable Stability Control
item.description: In these vehicles, a small part inside the brake pedal position sensor, called a capacitor, may develop a crack. This crack can cause the vehicle's electronic stability control to stop working while the vehicle is being driven. Dealers will inspect the brake pedal position sensor on affected vehicles and replace the sensor if a crack is found, and this repair will be done free of charge to the owner.

item.title: Tesla Model Y Front Suspension Connections May Loosen
item.description: Tesla is recalling certain Model Y vehicles because hardware securing one or more front suspension links may not have been tightened properly. A link could loosen or come away from the vehicle's supporting frame. Tesla Service will tighten or replace the securing hardware, check wheel alignment, and replace related parts that have been damaged if needed. The work is free.

item.title: Ford Mustang Wiring Can Cause Power Loss
item.description: The engine compartment wiring harness has ground connections that can crack or break over time. If that happens, the vehicle can lose the power that keeps it moving forward. The same wiring problem can also cause other systems to stop working, including the windshield washers, the headlights, the air conditioning, or the engine cooling fan, depending on which connection is affected.

item.title: Outlander Rearview Camera May Not Display
item.description: Mitsubishi is recalling certain Outlander and Outlander PHEV vehicles because of a software problem in the vehicle's infotainment system. Due to improper programming, the system may fail to show the rearview camera image on the screen when the vehicle is put into reverse. This means the driver may not be able to see the picture from the rearview camera while backing up, which does not meet federal rear visibility requirements.

item.title: Ford Bronco Sport Engine Pistons May Fail
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Bronco Sport vehicles because the tops of the engine pistons may have been made incorrectly. These piston tops can fail, causing the vehicle to unexpectedly lose power to keep moving. Dealers will inspect the pistons and replace the engine assembly if needed. Ford says additional owner letters will be sent when the repair becomes available, anticipated in December 2026.

item.title: Ford Bronco Sport Loose Joints May Fail
item.description: Ford is recalling certain Bronco Sport vehicles because some places where vehicle parts are joined may not be tightened properly. Parts could come loose or detach, cargo could become unsecured, and protection in a crash could be reduced. The problem can also cause electrical failure or make the vehicle unstable. Dealers will inspect these connections and tighten, repair, or replace the affected hardware as needed.

item.title: Kia EV9 air bag may not detect a child
item.description: Kia America is recalling certain 2025-2026 EV9 vehicles. Because of improper routing, the system meant to detect a child or child seat in the front passenger seat and turn off the air bag may not work as intended, so the air bag may not deactivate when it should.
